Thursday, Oct. 8: New CBS Legal Drama ‘Cupertino’ Takes on High-Stakes Cases in Silicon Valley

October 8, 2026 StayTuned Staff TV Best Bets

Thursday, Oct. 8

Cupertino
CBS, 10pm
New Series!
This new legal drama comes from the power producers of The Good Wife and Elsbeth. Set in the heart of Silicon Valley, the drama follows a lawyer (Mike Colter, Evil) who is being cheated out of his stock options by his former employer, a tech startup. Refusing to back down, he joins forces with another recently fired attorney (Rachel Keller) to represent those taken advantage of by the tech elite and help them fight back in a high-stakes battle against the Goliaths controlling Silicon Valley. Also stars Busy Philipps.

Below
Netflix
New Series!
Stay back from the water! “I really wanted to do something that felt like the old-school kind of handcrafted genre movies that also had a lot of character and a really strong sense of place and mood,” says creator Jesse McKeown of this new six-episode sea monster thriller. Josh Hartnett (Oppenheimer) stars as Calvin, a Newfoundland fisherman traumatized by his father’s mysterious death, and Charlie Heaton (Stranger Things) plays his son, Wade. Calvin is determined to keep his family safe from the creature terrorizing their small island town, which means teaming up with a visiting marine expert (Mackenzie Davis, Station Eleven). But it’s not just what’s under the water that they have to worry about. Their way of life is also vanishing.

Georgie & Mandy’s First Marriage
CBS, 8pm
Season Premiere!
The Young Sheldon spinoff is back for Season 3 with “Feminine Wiles and Some Tire Thing in Lubbock.” Tensions rise when Mandy (Emily Osment) and the family side against Georgie (Montana Jordan) in his fight with Mary (returning guest star Zoe Perry).

Scrabble: “X Marks the Bonus Square”
The CW, 8pm
Contestants hope their strong wordplay can help navigate them toward the final round and the $10,000 prize in the new episode “X Marks the Bonus Square.” Craig Ferguson hosts.

Hell’s Kitchen: “Sliding Into Hell”
FOX, 8pm
After an intense dinner final, the teams get a break with a day full of waterslides and burger sliders. The fun soon turns into a fierce slider stakeout competition judged by Paul Wahlberg, cofounder of Wahlburgers, in the new episode “Sliding Into Hell.”

The Traitors: New Blood: “Wake of the Living Dead”
NBC, 8pm
Pressure is at a boiling point as the Traitors must commit their next murder in plain sight. Meanwhile, the stakes are higher than ever for the players as they face a terrifying night that could change everything in the new episode “Wake of the Living Dead.”

Creepy Cinema: Desperate Survival
TCM, beginning at 8pm
Catch a Classic!
Two very different groups fight to make it through impossible circumstances tonight. First, Jane Fonda and Michael Sarrazin enter a grueling Depression-era dance marathon in They Shoot Horses, Don’t They? (1969). Next, Alfred Hitchcock showcases the action almost entirely at sea in Lifeboat (1944), where survivors of a torpedoed ship pull a German sailor aboard their small boat. Both films trap strangers together and show just how quickly fear and desperation can change people as they struggle to survive.

NFL Football: Tampa Bay at Dallas
Prime Video, 8:15pm Live
AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, hosts tonight’s Week 5 Thursday Night Football clash between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Dallas Cowboys.

Eternally Yours
CBS, 8:30pm
New Series!
The annoyances of a long-term marriage! The creators of Ghosts sink their teeth into another comedy winner, hilariously sharing modern-day family life for a coven of vampires. This is literally bloody fun, laugh-out-loud storytelling. After meeting her passionate vampire lover Charles (Ed Weeks) in 1526 Austria, mortal Liz (Allegra Edwards) begged him to turn her into a vampire so they could spend eternity together. Well, be careful of what you wish for, because living with someone for 20 years let alone 500 certainly takes some patience, and Liz has had just about enough. Thankfully, their extended coven that includes their daughter Emma (Helen J Shen) and trusted fitness-guru friend Jesse (Parker Young), along with his twin sons and elderly, non-vampire wife Phyllis (Rose Abdoo), provides plenty of distractions in their present-day Seattle habitat.

Elsbeth
CBS, 9pm
Season Premiere!
Elsbeth (Carrie Preston) crosses paths with renowned marriage counselor Serena Collyer (guest star Nicole Scherzinger), whose cool demeanor hides a murderous and messy passion. Gloria Reuben also reprises her guest role as Claudia Payne in the Season 4 premiere “Crazy in Love.”

Trivial Pursuit: “On the Road Again”
The CW, 9pm
A world traveler explores the six iconic Trivial Pursuit categories in hopes of winning $20,000 in the new episode “On the Road Again.” LeVar Burton hosts.

Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test: “Trust”
FOX, 9pm
In the new episode “Trust,” the recruits will brave their toughest obstacle yet: each other. In their first challenge, they pair off in a punishing round of hand-to-hand combat. Later, they must put the utmost trust in one another as their fate hangs off the steep edge of a cliff.

Law & Order: Special Victims Unit
NBC, 9pm
Season Premiere!
Mariska Hargitay returns as Capt. Olivia Benson for a heart-pounding 28th season of the longest-running scripted primetime drama series in television history. J. Smith-Cameron (Succession) has a recurring role this season as jury consultant Gwen Sharpe.

Law & Order
NBC, 10pm
Season Premiere!
The venerable crime drama starring Hugh Dancy, Tony Goldwyn, Maura Tierney and David Ajala is back for a 26th season. James Badge Dale (Hightown) is joining the main cast, while Reid Scott, who starred as Senior Detective Vincent Riley, appears in a few episodes this season to wrap his character’s story.

Get the latest from ReMIND Magazine!


Friday, Oct. 9

A Day Like No Other
Netflix
New Series!
This eight-episode biographical series recounts the life of Raphael, from his humble beginnings in post-war Spain to his conquest of the world’s greatest stages. The series portrays the unstoppable rise of a one-of-a-kind artist: his most intimate passions, his greatest hits, his personal struggles and the demons that have haunted him throughout his life. Set against backdrops ranging from Madrid to Las Vegas, via Moscow, Paris and Acapulco, A Day Like no Other is an emotional journey through five decades full of highs and lows. A moving story that reveals the man behind the legend.

Haunted Hotel
Netflix
Season Premiere!
Creator Matt Roller and others bring us a second season of this animated series that sees a single mother trying to run the world’s most haunted hotel with her ghost brother, two kids, a demon trapped in a little boy’s body, and an ever-growing collection of ghosts, monsters and supernatural disasters.

Matchbox The Movie
Apple TV
Original Film!
The massive success of Barbie (it ended up as the highest-grossing film of 2023) opened the floodgates for movies inspired by nostalgic Mattel toy brands. But how do you translate a series of tiny, die-cast cars into a major motion picture? “That’s a tough thing to do!” says director Sam Hargrave of the challenge. “We wanted to do something that captured the spirit of creativity and free play and making your own adventure that Matchbox toys are all about, but on a big scale.” That kind of scale was necessary for this bigtime action-adventure. The story follows Matchbox-loving former childhood friends whose lives are upended when their old leader Sean (John Cena), now a CIA operative, reappears and unwittingly gets them embroiled in a frantic international pursuit to save the world.

College Football
The CW, ESPN & FS1, beginning at 7pm Live
Friday night college football action features Florida State at Louisville (ESPN), Iowa at Washington (FS1), Washington State at Utah State (The CW) and Iowa State at BYU (ESPN).

Sheriff Country
CBS, 8pm
Season Premiere!
Sheriff Mickey Fox (Morena Baccarin) struggles to process a shocking revelation about her family in the Season 2 premiere “Cyclone.” Mickey also races to save a troubled young woman whose descent into a dangerous criminal operation uncovers a growing threat to all of Edgewater. Ben McKenzie, Baccarin’s husband, guest-stars as a sheriff from a neighboring town.

JAŸ-Z IN 8
HBO, 8pm
Series Finale!
Director Rick Rubin closes out this deeply revealing documentary portrait of JAŸ-Z and his work, exploring the influences and inspiration that shaped both the man and his music.

Boorman and the Devil
TCM, 8pm
Catch a Classic!
Go behind the scenes of one of Hollywood’s most infamous sequels with the TCM premiere of Boorman and the Devil, David Kittredge’s 2025 documentary about the making and reception of John Boorman’s Exorcist II: The Heretic (1977), which follows. Airing next are three more films directed by Boorman: the semi-biographical wartime drama Hope and Glory (1987), the tough crime thriller Point Blank (1967) and the South Africa-set drama In My Country (2004). It is a full night devoted to Boorman’s ambitious career.

Fire Country
CBS, 9pm
Season Premiere!
Max Thieriot is back as firefighter Bode Leone as Season 5 of the action drama debuts with “Founders’ Day.” As Edgewater celebrates its annual Founders’ Day festival, a catastrophic sinkhole opens beneath Main Street, trapping residents underground and forcing Station 42 into a high-stakes rescue.

Scariest House in America: “Scares of the Mysterious Midwest”
HGTV, 9pm
Retta’s journey to find scary takes her to the mysterious Midwest, where four homes contend for a chance at a stunning makeover by designer Alison Victoria. It’s between a ghostly home with a history of squatters, a Victorian full of ghosts and dolls, a historical haunt from the 1800s, and a large, creepy home that’s bananas.

The UnBelievable With Dan Aykroyd: “Peculiar Places”
History, 9pm
A bleeding house. A near-boiling river. A desert of unexplained encounters. OK, History, you have us on that bleeding house (no thanks on being neighbors to that!). Dan Aykroyd continues his exploration of some of the most peculiar places on Earth.

Austin City Limits: “Olivia Rodrigo”
PBS, 9pm
Singer-songwriter Olivia Rodrigo performs highlights from her 2026 album You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love.

Boston Blue
CBS, 10pm
Season Premiere!
The Blue Bloods spinoff returns for Season 2 with “The Crash,” as Danny and Lena (Donnie Wahlberg and Sonequa Martin-Green) race to stop a copycat killer inspired by the Boston Strangler.

Great Musicians of Our Time
PBS, 10pm
New Series!
This documentary series features six of the most influential and celebrated classical music artists of the 20th and 21st centuries. Witness Itzhak Perlman’s inspiring journey from young prodigy to icon in the premiere episode “Itzhak Perlman: Virtuoso Violinist.”

Saturday, Oct. 10

The Spirit of Halloween
Hallmark Channel, 8pm
Original Film!
Hallmark darling Meghan Ory plays Everly Stone, a woman who is very firmly anti-Halloween until she is visited by three friendly yet spooky spirits. The spirits help her rediscover her true self and see what she’s been missing all along.

The Monster She Married
Lifetime, 8pm
Original Film!
This film is based on the book Fatal Prescription: A Doctor Without Remorse by John Griffiths. Shelley Charalambous (Molly Saunders) has spent years building a life with Joseph (Matthew Morrison), the man she once trusted as her pediatrician, while also enduring the abuse and manipulation that has trapped her since she was a teenager. But when another one of Joseph’s teenage patients is murdered just days before testifying against him, Shelley is forced to face the dark truth of her marriage that she’s long avoided.

Two for One: Maggie Gyllenhaal
TCM, beginning at 8pm
Catch a Classic!
Actor and filmmaker Maggie Gyllenhaal presents a pair of acclaimed international films. Federico Fellini’s Nights of Cabiria (1957) stars Giulietta Masina as a Roman sex worker who keeps searching for love despite one disappointment after another. Next is Babette’s Feast (1987), which follows a French refugee who prepares an extraordinary meal for the members of a strict religious community in Denmark. The Danish film became the first movie from Denmark to win the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

48 Hours
CBS, 10pm
Season Premiere!
The newsmagazine investigating fascinating cases that touch on all aspects of the human experience returns for Season 39.

Saturday Night Live: “Shane Gillis/Rosalía”
NBC, 11:25pm Live
Actor and comedian Shane Gillis (Tires) hosts with Spanish singer-songwriter Rosalía as musical guest.

Sunday, Oct. 11

NFL Football
NBC & NFL Network, beginning at 9:30am Live
Enjoy an NFL game during Sunday breakfast as the Philadelphia Eagles face the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in England on NFL Network. The day’s action wraps up on NBC’s Sunday Night Football with the Baltimore Ravens at the Atlanta Falcons.

Marshals: “End of Watch”
CBS, 8pm
The Marshals close in on a former cop who launched a killing spree against those he blames for sabotaging his career in the new episode “End of Watch.”

MLB Playoffs: NL Championship Series: Game 1: L.A. Dodgers at Milwaukee
FOX or FS1, 8pm Live
Game 1 of the best-of-seven National League Championship Series takes place at American Family Field in Milwaukee, as the L.A. Dodgers face the Brewers in a rematch of the 2025 NLCS. FOX and FS1 split coverage of the series.

The Marlow Murder Club
PBS, 8pm
Season Finale!
Season 3 of the mystery drama wraps up with “An Appetite for Murder: Part Two.” As the police investigate the chef’s death, a shocking new development forces Judith (Samantha Bond), Becks (Cara Horgan) and Suzie (Jo Martin) to question their assumptions and rethink everything they have learned so far.

Starring John Boles
TCM, beginning at 8pm
Catch a Classic!
John Boles takes center stage in two films from the early 1930s. In Back Street (1932), he stars opposite Irene Dunne in the first film adaptation of Fannie Hurst’s novel about a woman who spends years in a painful relationship with a married man. Then, Boles lends his voice to the Technicolor musical revue King of Jazz (1930), built around bandleader Paul Whiteman and his orchestra.

Tracker: “Switchback”
CBS, 9pm
When a mother and daughter vanish while hiking the Pacific Divide Trail, Colter (Justin Hartley) races to find them after discovering they were being stalked in the new episode “Switchback.”

Marble Hall Murders
PBS, 9pm
Season Finale!
In the final chapter of this fiendish puzzle, both Susan (Lesley Manville) and Pünd (Tim McMullan) race against time to discover the truth. But can they solve these murders before the final page turns?

Trespasses
PBS, 10pm
Series Finale!
The limited drama series following the forbidden love affair between married Protestant barrister Michael (Tom Cullen) and Catholic schoolteacher Cushla (Lola Petticrew) during the Troubles in 1975 Northern Ireland concludes.

Monday, Oct. 12

Star of the Month: Myrna Loy
TCM, beginning at 7:30am
Catch a Classic!
Myrna Loy’s Star of the Month celebration moves through one especially busy year before settling in for a complete Thin Man marathon. The daytime schedule features eight of her films from 1932, including Love Me Tonight, Thirteen Women and The Mask of Fu Manchu. Tonight, Loy becomes Nora Charles opposite William Powell’s Nick in The Thin Man (1934). All five sequels follow, ending with Song of the Thin Man (1947). It is the perfect chance to watch one of classic Hollywood’s most beloved screen couples from beginning to end.

NFL Football: Buffalo at L.A. Rams
ABC & ESPN, 8pm Live
Two teams with Super Bowl aspirations meet at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, as the Buffalo Bills take on the L.A. Rams on Monday Night Football.

FBI: “Omissions”
CBS, 8pm
The team investigates a drug dealer suspected of murdering an NYPD officer in front of his daughter’s school in the new episode “Omissions.”

Private Eyes West Coast: “Shroom With a View”
The CW, 8pm
Shade (Jason Priestley) and Angie (Cindy Sampson) investigate the case of a university student who hasn’t returned from her hike and the threatening note left under her door.

Celebrity Name That Tune: “It’s a ’90s Halloween”
FOX, 8pm
In the new “It’s a ’90s Halloween” episode, TV icons from the 1990s collide as Beverly Hills 90210’s Brian Austin Green takes on Melrose Place’s Daphne Zuniga. Then, paranormal investigator Emily takes on supernatural writer Victoria. Jane Krakowski hosts with bandleader Robin Thicke.

MLB Playoffs: AL Championship Series: Game 1: Chicago/Cleveland at Tampa Bay
TBS & truTV, 8pm Live
The American League champion will be determined by a best-of-seven series beginning with Game 1 tonight at Tropicana Field, home of the Tampa Bay Rays. The Rays will face either the Chicago White Sox or the Cleveland Guardians. TBS and truTV air all ALCS games.

CIA: “Dead Drop”
CBS, 9pm
A Russian spy poisoned by his own comrades seeks revenge and offers to help the CIA team neutralize a threat against U.S. assets in the new episode “Dead Drop.”

Law & Order Toronto: Criminal Intent: “Digital Lipstick”
The CW, 9pm
Graff and Bateman (Aden Young and Kathleen Munroe) are called to investigate when a tech professional is stabbed to death at a drug store in the new episode “Digital Lipstick.”

Celebrity Weakest Link: “Fright Night”
FOX, 9pm
Get ready to scream as horror legends from The Exorcist, A Nightmare on Elm Street, American Horror Story and others face off in the new episode “Fright Night.” Jane Lynch hosts.

It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia
FX & FXX, 9pm
Season Finale!
“The Guys Have a Sleepover” sounds like a delightful way to wrap up Season 18 of the comedy following the Paddy’s Pub Gang’s misadventures. Rob Mac, Charlie Day, Kaitlin Olson, Glenn Howerton and Danny DeVito star.

Harlan Coben’s Final Twist: “A Mother’s Crusade”
CBS, 10pm
The true-crime series continues with the new episode “A Mother’s Crusade.” A mother fights to reopen the investigation into her daughter’s disappearance and death, convinced there was foul play involved in what was initially ruled a hiking accident.

Line of Fire: “Paper Trails”
NBC, 10pm
Clare (Kat Cunning) investigates a wedding bomb threat against a cabinet member in the new episode “Paper Trails.”

VOCES: “Paquito D’Rivera — From Carne y Frijol to Carnegie Hall”
PBS, 10pm
This new installment in the VOCES documentary series celebrates the life and legacy of Latin jazz legend Paquito D’Rivera, including his journey from child prodigy in Cuba to a career as a Grammy-winning musician and composer.

Tuesday, Oct. 13

Laraine Day Birthday Tribute
TCM, beginning at 7am
Catch a Classic!
TCM celebrates Laraine Day’s birthday with films spanning more than a decade of her career. The day begins with Calling Dr. Kildare (1939), one of several entries in which Day played nurse Mary Lamont. Other highlights include Alfred Hitchcock’s Foreign Correspondent (1940), the wartime drama Journey for Margaret (1942), Mr. Lucky (1943) with Cary Grant and the psychological noir The Locket (1946). The film tribute closes with The Woman on Pier 13 (1949), which was originally titled I Married a Communist.

NHL Hockey
ESPN, beginning at 6pm Live
ESPN gives hockey fans a big Tuesday night NHL tripleheader with the New Jersey Devils at the Detroit Red Wings, the Colorado Avalanche at the Dallas Stars and the Boston Bruins at the San Jose Sharks.

NCIS: “Clean Slate”
CBS, 8pm
When a man is murdered after a neighborhood dinner party, the team discovers every guest is lying about what transpired in the new episode “Clean Slate.”

Best Medicine: “No Place Like Om”
FOX, 8pm
In the new episode “No Place Like Om,” Martin (Josh Charles) desperately tries to leave Port Wenn for a weekend trip to Boston, but he must first investigate the extremely strange behavior of three patients who have all recently visited a meditation retreat.

A Very Haunted Renovation: “The Exterior Exorcism”
HGTV, 8pm
And then there were three! For the first time in this new series hosted by Anna Camp, the three remaining designers tackle a space of their own as they transform Bihl Manor’s neglected exterior. Battling the spirits and the elements, they’re aiming to give the grounds a glow-up worthy of the judges.

NCIS: New York: “Family Business”
CBS, 9pm
In the new episode “Family Business,” the team is called in to find the suspect behind a deadly jewelry store robbery that involved military explosives.

Doc: “Great Expectations”
FOX, 9pm
Amy and Ben (Molly Parker and Blair Underwood) are at odds when their cancer patient demands the impossible in the new episode “Great Expectations.”

R.J. Decker: “Better Luck Tomorrow”
ABC, 10pm
R.J. (Scott Speedman) and his dad must discover who has been gaslighting the caretaker at a senior living community and unwind a murderous scheme that has R.J.’s client convinced he’s living the same day in a loop.

NCIS: Origins: “My Own Worst Enemy”
CBS, 10pm
In the new episode “My Own Worst Enemy,” present-day Gibbs (returning guest star Mark Harmon) returns to civilization and calls in a favor from old friend Woody (guest star Bobby Moynihan). In 1992, the team bands together to help Woody when he’s accused of murdering a bowling rival.

Frontline: “American Voices 2026”
PBS, 10pm
The new episode “American Voices 2026” explores the changing views and experiences of Americans from the 2020 election to today, revealing how the hopes and fears of voters first filmed six years ago have changed amid another polarizing election season.

Wednesday, Oct. 14

Scrubs: “My Chief”
ABC, 8pm
In the new episode “My Chief,” J.D. (Zach Braff) discovers that Turk (Donald Faison) made a costly mistake and has to decide whether to report it or let it slide.

The Floor: “The Quiet Achiever”
FOX, 8pm
A millionaire champion takes the Floor by surprise before a David vs. Goliath battle reduces the champion to tears in the new episode “The Quiet Achiever.” Rob Lowe hosts.

MLB Playoffs: NL Championship Series: Game 3: Milwaukee at L.A. Dodgers
FOX or FS1, 8pm Live
The best-of-seven National League Championship Series moves to Dodger Stadium for Game 3 as the Milwaukee Brewers take on the Dodgers.

Pawn Stars: “Fangs for the Memories”
History, 8pm
Rick Harrison checks out some basketball cards that reheat the Magic Johnson and Larry Bird rivalry; he and Chum take a field trip to look at some high-end watches; and rare books expert Rebecca Romney sinks her teeth into a first printing of Dracula.

Chicago Med: “Third Rails”
NBC, 8pm
Subway surfers enter the E.D. with serious injuries and Charles (Oliver Platt) looks to solve a mysterious case in the new episode “Third Rails.”

Nature
PBS, 8pm
Season Premiere!
Join Elmo and the Sesame Street gang on a once-in-a-lifetime African safari adventure in this episode presented in collaboration with Sesame Workshop. After adopting an orphaned elephant online, Elmo, Abby and Nina travel to Kenya to meet the young elephant and the keepers who care for her. They’ll also see some of nature’s most iconic wildlife, including lions, zebras, giraffes and hippos.

Monty Python Triple Feature
TCM, beginning at 8pm
Catch a Classic!
Spend the evening with the Monty Python troupe and three of its feature films. Monty Python and the Holy Grail (1975) sends King Arthur and his knights on a wildly silly quest. Monty Python’s Life of Brian (1979) follows a man born next door to Jesus who is repeatedly mistaken for the Messiah. The night ends with Monty Python’s The Meaning of Life (1983), an irreverent series of sketches about life, death and nearly everything in between.

Abbott Elementary: “Check-Ins”
ABC, 8:30pm
Gregory (Tyler James Williams) juggles the demands of his two roles, while Jacob and Melissa (Chris Perfetti and Lisa Ann Walter) struggle to compromise in the new episode “Check-Ins.”

99 to Beat: “It’s All About the Balance”
FOX, 9pm
In the new episode “It’s All About the Balance,” 63 contestants remain to compete in five seemingly simple and hilarious games. Erin Andrews and Ken Jeong host.

The Lowdown
FX, 9pm ET/6pm PT
Season Premiere!
When Ethan Hawke’s Lee Raybon, Tulsa’s “truthstorian,” returns for Season 2 of Sterlin Harjo’s unique noir, he’s getting a bit too much praise for the murder mystery his investigative journalism solved in Season 1. Lee is having “an existential crisis about the meaninglessness of ‘success,’” says Hawke. “He has a desire to blow it up.” He distracts himself by helping public defender Ginger (Betty Gilpin) locate a missing client. “Lee is an unreliable friend, but he’s the only friend she has,” Hawke notes. Also exciting: Actor Tommy Lee Jones steps in as Hawke’s onscreen father, Lee Raybon Sr.

Chicago Fire: “Rattle the Cage”
NBC, 9pm
In the new episode “Rattle the Cage,” Violet and Novak (Hanako Greensmith and Jocelyn Hudon) grow suspicious of a mental health facility after treating an escaped patient.

NOVA: “Evolution: Brain Power”
PBS, 9pm
NOVA presents this fascinating five-part series about evolution. Each episode is rooted in the remarkable story of a different animal and uses it as a jumping-off point to chronicle how Earth’s inhabitants — including humans — have changed over eons. The premiere, “Brain Power,” traces the development of the brain, following the dolphin from 3 billion years ago to becoming one of the smartest animals alive today. It’s all enhanced by cinematic photography and animations of long-lost ancestors.

Chicago P.D.: “Don’t Blink”
NBC, 10pm
A significant turning point in Atwater’s (LaRoyce Hawkins) life prompts him to make a decision about his future in the new episode “Don’t Blink.”

Secrets of the Dead: “Africa’s Golden City”
PBS, 10pm
Built between the 11th and 15th centuries, Great Zimbabwe was one of the most prominent ancient civilizations of the African continent. It was the thriving capital of a massive trading empire, but for hundreds of years, Great Zimbabwe was dismissed by European explorers. The archaeological discoveries revealed in this new episode show the true scope of the ancient city’s global importance.

Thursday, Oct. 15

9-1-1
ABC, 8pm
Season Premiere!
The drama series about the high-pressure experiences of Los Angeles first responders — including police officers, firefighters and dispatchers — who are thrust into the most frightening, shocking and heart-stopping situations is back for Season 10 with “That Sinking Feeling.” Angela Bassett, Aisha Hinds and Jennifer Love Hewitt star.

Georgie & Mandy’s First Marriage: “A Serious Journalist and Your Brain on Drugs”
CBS, 8pm
Mandy’s (Emily Osment) work dinner goes awry when Georgie (Montana Jordan) gets distracted by a surprise encounter in the new episode “A Serious Journalist and Your Brain on Drugs.”

Scrabble: “Vowel Language”
The CW, 8pm
Three wordsmiths put their vocabulary skills to the test as they compete for a chance at the $10,000 prize in the new episode “Vowel Language.” Craig Ferguson hosts.

Hell’s Kitchen: “Hell’s Kitchen University”
FOX, 8pm
The chefs get a glimpse of college life and compete in a beer pong challenge to decide who can best pair alcohol with their protein in the new episode “Hell’s Kitchen University.”

The Traitors: New Blood: “A Murder of Necessity”
NBC, 8pm
Shaken by the funeral, the Faithful conspire to solve who committed the murder in plain sight in the new episode “A Murder of Necessity.”

NFL Football: Seattle at Denver
Prime Video, 8:15pm Live
The Seattle Seahawks face the Broncos in Denver to kick off Week 6 on Thursday Night Football.

Eternally Yours: “Baby Vampire”
CBS, 8:30pm
Max (Jaren Lewison) and Emma (Helen J. Shen) try to process their new reality, while Charles (Ed Weeks) attempts to make a friend at work in the new episode “Baby Vampire.”

9-1-1: Nashville
ABC, 9pm
Season Premiere!
The 9-1-1 spinoff set in Nashville returns for Season 2 with “Going Rogue,” as the Music City’s heroic first responders face new professional and personal challenges. Chris O’Donnell, Jessica Capshaw and Kimberly Williams-Paisley star.

Elsbeth: “Death of a Playwright”
CBS, 9pm
When a young playwright’s suspicious death rocks the world of New York theater, Elsbeth (Carrie Preston) finds several suspects waiting in the wings. Nicholas Braun (Succession) guest-stars in the new episode “Death of a Playwright.”

Trivial Pursuit: “Jimmy Eat Trivia”
The CW, 9pm
A game-show enthusiast takes on the six iconic Trivial Pursuit categories in hopes of winning $20,000 in the new episode “Jimmy Eat Trivia.” LeVar Burton hosts.

Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test: “Leadership”
FOX, 9pm
In the new episode “Leadership,” some recruits are challenged to lead their team in a hostage rescue in a race against time. Tensions rise when the recruits must infiltrate an enemy compound to gather information while under a powerful gas attack.

Law & Order: Special Victims Unit: “Midway”
NBC, 9pm
In the new episode “Midway,” Curry (Aimé Donna Kelly) answers a family’s call for help when their son disappears from a carnival. The search uncovers a chilling connection to an old abduction and a tragic chain of events.

Grey’s Anatomy
ABC, 10pm
Season Premiere!
The drama following the doctors, nurses and staff at Grey Sloan Memorial returns in the Season 23 premiere “Collide.” Ellen Pompeo, Chandra Wilson and James Pickens Jr. star.

Cupertino: “Vik & Bo”
CBS, 10pm
In the new episode “Vik & Bo,” Michael and Olivia (Mike Colter and Rachel Keller) defend Vik Malhotra (Nik Dodani), a Silicon Valley coder being held responsible for an errant drone that killed an onlooker during an elaborate drone display.

Law & Order: “Into the Mystic”
NBC, 10pm
Price and Walker (Hugh Dancy and David Ajala) are forced off a high-stakes case when their connection to a murder suspect creates a conflict of interest in the new episode “Into the Mystic.”

Creepy Cinema Classic Monsters
TCM, beginning at 12:45am (late night)
Catch a Classic!
The lineup begins with The Brides of Dracula (1960) and Blood From the Mummy’s Tomb (1971), followed by Christopher Lee in Dracula Has Risen From the Grave (1968). Lee and Peter Cushing reunite in Dracula A.D. 1972 (1972), which brings their famous rivalry to modern London. The marathon continues with The Curse of Frankenstein (1957), Horror of Dracula (1958) and The Mummy (1959), three films that helped define Hammer Productions’ colorful Gothic style.

Friday, Oct. 16

College Football
ESPN, ESPN2 & FOX, beginning at 12pm Live
Catch Memphis at Tulane (ESPN), Washington at Purdue (FOX) and Appalachian State at Coastal Carolina (ESPN2) in Friday night’s college football matchups.

Sheriff Country: “Family Trust”
CBS, 8pm
A breakthrough in a 30-year-old cold case forces a family to confront a long-buried secret in the new episode “Family Trust.”

Tis the Season for Setups
Hallmark Channel, 8pm
Original Film!
Hyper-organized single mom and party planner Lexi (Amanda Schull), her free-spirited mother June (Barbara Niven) and teen daughter Piper (Verity Marks) are set to spend Christmas at a local ski resort after Lexi is hired to organize their annual holiday party. Upon arrival, she immediately butts heads with Ridge (Victor Webster), the ski instructor and son of the lodge’s owner, Dan (John B. Lowe). Looks like some matchmaking could be in store.

Becoming Hitchcock: The Legacy of Blackmail
TCM, 8pm
Catch a Classic!
This night devoted to Alfred Hitchcock and four of his memorable leading women starts with the 2024 documentary Becoming Hitchcock: The Legacy of Blackmail, which explores the director’s signature style through the making of the 1929 film Blackmail. Following is the sound version of Blackmail, starring Anny Ondra, and The 39 Steps (1935), with Madeleine Carroll. Grace Kelly takes over later in Dial M for Murder (1954), while Eva Marie Saint joins Cary Grant in North by Northwest (1959). A 2014 TCM festival conversation with Saint closes the lineup.

Fire Country: “Fire Under Fire”
CBS, 9pm
When a fast-moving wildfire threatens Edgewater, Station 42 and Three Rock battle increasingly dangerous conditions in an effort to contain the blaze in the new episode “Fire Under Fire.”

Scariest House in America: “Nightmares in New England”
HGTV, 9pm
Retta’s journey to find scary takes her to nightmarish New England, where four homes battle for a chance at a stunning makeover by designer Alison Victoria. It’s between a large house with whistling and humming specters, a diabolical duplex, a former jailhouse, and a gigantic house with a mind of its own.

The UnBelievable With Dan Aykroyd: “Incredible Spectacles”
History, 9pm
From donkey baseball and octopus wrestling to a scientist who swallows uranium, host Dan Aykroyd shares these jaw-dropping spectacles that left crowds in awe.

Boston Blue: “Ripple Effect”
CBS, 10pm
As Danny and Lena (Donnie Wahlberg and Sonequa Martin-Green) follow a lead in a case, they find themselves in an intense standoff with a dangerous biker gang in the new episode “Ripple Effect.”

Great Musicians of Our Time: “Pinchas Zukerman: Here to Make Music”
PBS, 10pm
This documentary series profiling six of the most influential and celebrated classical music artists of the 20th and 21st centuries continues with “Pinchas Zukerman: Here to Make Music.” Israeli American violinist, conductor and music master Zukerman’s legacy continues to inspire after more than five decades.

The Rainmaker
USA Network, 10pm
Season Premiere!
The first season, based on John Grisham’s novel, ended with Rudy (Milo Callaghan) and Deck (P.J. Byrne) winning millions for their client thanks to some unusual and lowbrow legal tactics. Now armed with heaps of cash, “they’re hounded by high-profile, high-paying clients,” Callaghan tells. In-demand though they may be, “they’re still dysfunctional, still in a Taco Hut and still moving like scrappy underdogs,” he adds. Season 2 will explore life before Rudy joined Bruiser’s (Lana Parrilla) ragtag team, but one thing that’s not likely to happen is a rekindling of the romance between Rudy and Sarah (Madison Iseman).

Saturday, Oct. 17

College Football
ABC, ESPN & FOX, beginning at 12pm
Catch Ohio State at Indiana (FOX), Arizona State at Texas Tech (FOX), Florida State at Miami (ESPN), Notre Dame at BYU (ABC) and Oklahoma State at Houston (FOX) in Saturday’s top college football action.

WNBA Finals: Game 1
NBC, 3:30pm Live
The best-of-seven-game WNBA Finals tip off today on the home court of the conference champion with the better regular-season record.

Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story
Hallmark Channel, 8pm
Original Film!
The Chicago Bears take center stage for Hallmark’s next Holiday Touchdown franchise film. The love story will feature cameo appearances from Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson, tight ends Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet, and legendary Bears alumni Mike Singletary, Charles “Peanut” Tillman and Dan Hampton. Connie Payton, wife of the late legendary running back Walter Payton, and the team’s beloved mascot Staley Da Bear will also bring a little extra football spirit to the holiday romance.

Sins of an Amish Husband
Lifetime, 8pm
Original Film!
Inspired by real events and adapted from Gregg Olsen’s acclaimed true-crime book Abandoned Prayers, this film follows Sarah (Maddy Hillis), a woman of Amish faith, who suspects foul play when her sister Ida (Karis Cameron) tragically dies in a mysterious barn fire.

Two for One: Colman Domingo
TCM, beginning at 8pm
Catch a Classic!
Actor Colman Domingo shares two selections tonight, beginning with one of Alfred Hitchcock’s most enduring thrillers. Rear Window (1954) stars James Stewart as an injured photographer who becomes convinced that one of his neighbors has committed murder, with Grace Kelly as the girlfriend who helps him investigate. Immediately following, Paper Moon (1973) pairs Ryan O’Neal with his daughter Tatum O’Neal as two Depression-era con artists traveling through the Midwest. Tatum was 10 when she won the Best Supporting Actress Oscar for the role, making her the youngest competitive acting winner in Academy Awards history.

Silver Bells at Christmas
Great American Family, 8pm
Original Film!
When Ginny fights to save her late mother’s beloved Christmas shop, a determined buyer and the return of her first love force her to choose between holding onto the past and opening her heart to a new future. Stars Laura Osnes, Ryan McPartlin, Chuck Wicks and Taylor Kalupa.

Austin City Limits: “Ari Lennox”
PBS, 11pm
In tonight’s new episode, R&B singer-songwriter Ari Lennox performs songs from her 2026 album Vacancy, alongside fan favorite songs like “Soft Girl Era” and “Shea Butter Baby.”
